STUDYQURAN:7:intro/r20.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:intro/r20.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:intro/r20.claim: Verses 104–126 give one of the Quran's most detailed accounts of Moses confronting Pharaoh and the sorcerers.
STUDYQURAN:7:intro/r20.anchor:
most
detailed accounts of Moses’ confrontation with Pharaoh and the sorcerers (vv. 104–26)

BURSEVI:v3p161#4/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p161#4/r4.speaker: السحرة
BURSEVI:v3p161#4/r4.claim: The converts say they will return to their Lord through death regardless of Pharaoh’s threat, or to His mercy and reward if he carries it out; they welcome meeting God.
BURSEVI:v3p161#4/r4.anchor: إلى ربنا منقلبون} راجعون ، أي : بالموت لا محالة سواء كان ذلك من قبلك

BURSEVI:v3p161#4/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p161#4/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p161#4/r5.claim: The Persian Mathnawi depicts souls freed from body as dancing in divine love and receiving revelations after the bodily veil is lifted.
BURSEVI:v3p161#4/r5.anchor:
جانهاى بسته اندر آب وكل
ون رهند ازآب وكلها شاد دلدرهواى عشق حق رقصان شوند

BURSEVI:v3p161#4/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p161#4/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p161#4/r6.claim: Their question “what do you resent in us?” means Pharaoh has no fault to criticize except their belief.
BURSEVI:v3p161#4/r6.anchor: {وما تنقم منآ} أي : وما تنكر وما تعيب منا.

BURSEVI:v3p161#5/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p161#5/r1.speaker: السحرة
BURSEVI:v3p161#5/r1.claim: The magicians say their sole offense is believing in God’s signs when they arrived, the best deed and root of virtue, which they will not abandon to please Pharaoh.
BURSEVI:v3p161#5/r1.anchor: {إلا أن ءامنا بآيات ربنا لما جآءتنا} وهو خير الأعمال وأصل المناقب

BURSEVI:v3p161#5/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p161#5/r2.speaker: السحرة
BURSEVI:v3p161#5/r2.claim: They pray for patience that will overwhelm them like poured water as they face Pharaoh’s threat; the image is a concealed simile elaborated through metaphor.
BURSEVI:v3p161#5/r2.anchor: {ربنآ أفرغ علينا صبرا} أي : أفض علينا من الصبر على وعيد فرعون ما يغمرنا

BURSEVI:v3p161#5/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p161#5/r3.speaker: السحرة
BURSEVI:v3p161#5/r3.claim: They ask to die steadfast in the Islam God granted them, without being seduced by threats.
BURSEVI:v3p161#5/r3.anchor: {وتوفنا مسلمين} ثابتين على ما رزقتنا من الإسلام غير مفتونين من الوعيد

BURSEVI:v3p161#5/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p161#5/r4.speaker: قيل
BURSEVI:v3p161#5/r4.claim: A report says Pharaoh could not overpower them because God had promised Moses and Aaron victory over their followers.
BURSEVI:v3p161#5/r4.anchor: قيل لم يقدر عليهم لقوله تعالى : {أنتما ومن اتبعكما الغالبون}

BURSEVI:v3p161#5/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p161#5/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
BURSEVI:v3p161#5/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas reports that Pharaoh seized the magicians, cut them apart, and crucified them on the Nile bank.
BURSEVI:v3p161#5/r5.anchor: وقال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : فأخذ فرعون السحرة فقطعهم ثم صلبهم على شاطىء نيل مصر.

BURSEVI:v3p161#5/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p161#5/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p161#5/r6.claim: The Mathnawi says the magicians knew the truth of God and surrendered their hands to the resulting punishment.
BURSEVI:v3p161#5/r6.anchor:
ساحران ون حق او بشناختند
دست وا در جرمها در باختند

BURSEVI:v3p161#5/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p161#5/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p161#5/r7.claim: Inwardly, Pharaoh is the ego that objects to the spirit’s faith, accusing the soul’s faculties of believing before permission and conspiring with the spirit.
BURSEVI:v3p161#5/r7.anchor: وفي القصة : إشارة إلى أن فرعون النفس أيضا منكر على إيمان سحرة صفاتها

BURSEVI:v3p162/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p162/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p162/r1.claim: In the inward reading, the city is the body and its inhabitants are bodily pleasures; when the soul’s qualities side with the spirit, worldly pleasures leave the body.
BURSEVI:v3p162/r1.anchor: {فى المدينة} مدينة القالب والبدن {لتخرجوا منهآ أهلها} وهو اللذات والشهوات البدنية الجسمانية

BURSEVI:v3p162/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p162/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p162/r2.claim: The ego threatens to defeat the virtues and recover bodily pleasures; it cuts their limbs from good works with the knife of false suggestion and crucifies them on worldly attachments.
BURSEVI:v3p162/r2.anchor: {لاقطعن أيديكم وأرجلكم من خلاف} بسكين التسويل عن الأعمال الصالحة.

BURSEVI:v3p162/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p162/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p162/r3.claim: The soul’s qualities answer that they return to God rather than the world, seeking patience through severing worldly attachments and death in servitude.
BURSEVI:v3p162/r3.anchor:
في جذوع تعلقات الدنيا وزخارفها.
{قالوا إنآ إلى ربنا منقلبون} لا إلى الدنيا وما فيها

AKHFASH:v1p335/r1.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p335/r1.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p335/r1.claim: نقم منا and تنقم منا represent two dialects, نقم ينقم and نقم ينقم; al-Akhfash reads the first form.
AKHFASH:v1p335/r1.anchor: وقال {وما تنقم منآ} وقال بعضهم {وما تنقم منا} وهما لغتان "نقم" "ينقم" و"نقم" "ينقم" وبها نقرأ. أي بالأولى.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p170#9/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p170#9/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p170#9/r1.claim: أفرغ علينا صبرا means pour patience over us.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p170#9/r1.anchor: أفرغ علينا صبرا} أي صبه علينا

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1538/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1538/r1.speaker: ابن عباس، السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1538/r1.claim: They were magicians in the morning and martyrs by evening.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1538/r1.anchor: عن السدى قال : قال عبد الله بن عباس : حين قالوا : ربنا افرغ علينا صبرا وتوفنا مسلمين قال : فكانوا في اول النهار سحرة ، وفي اخر النهار شهداء .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p54#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p54#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p54#2/r6.claim: They say Pharaoh has no reason to punish them except their faith in the signs once they saw them.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p54#2/r6.anchor: فإنك لا تعرف لنا سببا يوجب العقوبة غير ذلك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p56/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p56/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p56/r1.claim: Naqama means to object to an act, hate it, or resent its doer, by speech or action; it can follow two verb patterns, the first more eloquent, and all reciters use the form with a kasra on qāf.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p56/r1.anchor: والنقم : بسكون القاف وبفتحها ، الإنكار على الفعل ، وكراهة صدوره وحقد على فاعله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p56/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p56/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p56/r2.claim: The exception for believing is connected: faith is precisely what Pharaoh resents, so it is not a seeming contradiction.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p56/r2.anchor: والاستثناء في قولهم : { إلا أن آمنا بآيات ربنا } متصل ، لأن الإيمان ينقمه فرعون عليهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p56/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p56/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p56/r3.claim: Their prayer turns from addressing Pharaoh to addressing God, asking for capacity to endure his threat; pouring patience pictures exceptional strength through a hidden vessel metaphor, imagined pouring, and an implication of filling completely.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p56/r3.anchor: فشه الصبر بماء تشبيه المعقول بالمحسوس ، على طريقة الاستعارة المكنية ، وشبه خلقه في نفوسهم بإفراغ الماء من الإناء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p56/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p56/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p56/r4.claim: Asking to die as Muslims shows no desire for worldly life, confidence in the afterlife, and disregard for Pharaoh's threat; God may have spared them worldly disgrace, though the Quran omits the threat's fulfillment to emphasize God's support, their guidance, and steadfast faith.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p56/r4.anchor: ودعوا لأنفسهم بالوفاة على الإسلام إيذانا بأنهم غير راغبين في الحياة ، ولا مبالين بوعيد فرعون

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p440#3/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p440#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p440#3/r1.claim: The believing magicians submit themselves to God and rely on Him with confidence in what He has prepared.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p440#3/r1.anchor: هذا تسليم من مؤمني السحرة، واتكال على الله، وثقة بما عنده

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p440#3/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p440#3/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p440#3/r2.claim: Most read tanqimu with kasra on qāf; a group including Abu Haywa, Ibn Abi ʿAbla, and al-Hasan read it with fatḥa, two dialects. Abu Hatim prefers kasra; Ibn al-Ruqayyat’s line uses fatḥa.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p440#3/r2.anchor: وقرأ جمهور الناس «تنقم» بكسر القاف، وقرأ أبو حيوة وأبو البرهسم وابن أبي عبلة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p440#3/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p440#3/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p440#3/r3.claim: Mā tanqimu minnā means what fault do you charge us with or punish us for; afrigh ʿalaynā ṣabran is a metaphor of covering us with patience like poured water.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p440#3/r3.anchor: ومعناه وما تعد علينا ذنبا وتؤاخذنا به؟ وقولهم أفرغ علينا صبرا معناه عمنا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p440#3/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p440#3/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p440#3/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says six hundred thousand Israelites followed Moses after the magicians believed; al-Naqqash reports Muqatil’s view that Moses stayed in Egypt about a year showing signs.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p440#3/r4.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: لما آمنت السحرة اتبع موسى ستمائة ألف من بني إسرائيل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p243#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p243#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p243#2/r1.claim: The sorcerers tell Pharaoh he resents nothing in them except that they believed.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p243#2/r1.anchor: وما تكره منا شيئا ولا تعطن علينا إلا لأنا آمنا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p243#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p243#2/r2.speaker: مجاهد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p243#2/r2.claim: Mujahid says their prayer for patience asks for endurance through amputation and crucifixion so they will not revert to unbelief.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p243#2/r2.anchor: على القطع والصلب حتى لا نرجع كفارا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p243#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p243#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p243#2/r3.claim: Their request to die as Muslims means to remain sincere upon Moses’ religion.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p458#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p458#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p458#2/r1.claim: Pharaoh accuses the magicians of conspiring with Moses to seize power, expel the leaders, and control the city, then says they will see what he does to them.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p458#2/r1.anchor: أي: تجتمعوا أنتم وهو، وتكون لكم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p458#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p458#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p458#2/r4.claim: The magicians know they will return to God, whose punishment is harsher than Pharaoh's; they will endure Pharaoh's torture to escape God's punishment and seek steadfastness in Moses' religion.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p458#2/r4.anchor: قد تحققنا أنا إليه راجعون، وعذابه أشد من عذابك

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p458#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p458#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس وعبيد بن عمير وقتادة وابن جريج
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p458#2/r5.claim: The magicians were sorcerers in the morning and steadfast martyrs by evening after asking for patience and death as Muslims.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p458#2/r5.anchor: كانوا في أول النهار سحرة، وفي آخره شهداء

JISHUMI:v4p2675/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2675/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2675/r4.claim: Pouring patience is likened to emptying a vessel; patience is holding oneself through hardship. God should not be called ‘patient’; Abu ʿAli rejects al-Ṣabūr unless a report is sound, then explains it as forbearance.
JISHUMI:v4p2675/r4.anchor: وأفرغ علينا صبرا شبه بحال إفراغ الإناء كما يقال: صب عليه صبا.

JISHUMI:v4p2675/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2675/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2675/r5.claim: إنا is contracted from إننا by deleting one nūn; Rabbana is parsed as a vocative with annexation.
JISHUMI:v4p2675/r5.anchor: أصل (إنا) (إننا)، فإذا قيل: (إننا)، فقد ورد على أصل

MUQATIL:7:124-129/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:7:124-129/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:7:124-129/r2.claim: The magicians accept that they return to God and say Pharaoh resents only their belief in the signs of the hand and staff; they ask patience through mutilation and crucifixion, remaining sincere Muslims.
MUQATIL:7:124-129/r2.anchor: يعنى صدقنا باليد والعصا آيتان من ربنا،

MUQATIL:7:124-129/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:7:124-129/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:7:124-129/r3.claim: Pharaoh crucified the magicians that same day; they were unbelieving sorcerers at dawn and Muslim martyrs by evening after believing Moses.
MUQATIL:7:124-129/r3.anchor: فصلبهم فرعون من يومه، فكانوا أول النهار سحرة كفارا، وآخر النهار شهداء مسلمين

NASAFI-FULL:v2p30#9/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p30#9/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p30#9/r1.claim: The only supposed fault Pharaoh can find in them is faith, which is actually the source of honor and distinction; the poet similarly calls sword-wear the sole blemish of warriors.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p30#9/r1.anchor: وما تعيب منا إلا ما هو أصل المناقب والمفاخر وهو الإيمان ومنه قوله ولا عيب فيهم غير أن سيوفهم

NASAFI-FULL:v2p30#9/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p30#9/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p30#9/r2.claim: Their prayer asks for wide, abundant patience, as if it were poured over and flooded them.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p30#9/r2.anchor: أى اصبب صبا ذريعا والمعنى هب لنا صبرا واسعا واكثره علينا حتى يفيض علنا ويغمرنا

NASAFI-FULL:v2p30#9/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p30#9/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p30#9/r3.claim: They ask to die as Muslims, meaning steadfast in Islam.

RAZI-FULL:v14p170/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v14p170/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v14p170/r4.claim: A second argument for execution is that the magicians' plea for patience implies severe suffering; the counterargument is that they sought steadfastness in faith against Pharaoh's threat.
RAZI-FULL:v14p170/r4.anchor: والثاني : أن قوله تعالى حكاية عنهم { ربنا أفرغ علينا صبرا } يدل على أنه كان قد نزل بهم بلاء شديد عظيم

RAZI-FULL:v14p170/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v14p170/r6.speaker: آخرون
RAZI-FULL:v14p170/r6.claim: Others say the threat was not carried out and God answered their prayer to die Muslims, meaning their death came from God rather than execution; the author calls this inference close.
RAZI-FULL:v14p170/r6.anchor: وقال آخرون : إنه لم يقع من فرعون ذلك ، بل استجاب الله تعالى لهم الدعاء في قولهم : { وتوفنا مسلمين } لأنهم سألوه تعالى أن يكون توفيهم من جهته

RAZI-FULL:v14p170/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v14p170/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v14p170/r7.claim: Their answer models the best response to a threat: they say Pharaoh resents only that they believed the manifest signs, which should lead him to follow truth and avoid falsehood.
RAZI-FULL:v14p170/r7.anchor: فبينوا أن الذي كان منهم لا يوجب الوعيد ولا إنزال النقمة بهم ، بل يقتضي خلاف ذلك

RAZI-FULL:v14p170/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v14p170/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v14p170/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains that their only supposed offense was believing in the signs God sent through Moses, miracles only God could produce.
RAZI-FULL:v14p170/r8.anchor: قال ابن عباس : يريد ما أتينا بذنب تعذبنا عليه إلا أن آمنا بآيات ربنا

RAZI-FULL:v14p170/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v14p170/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v14p170/r9.claim: The verb naqima means to show intense aversion or hatred toward something.
RAZI-FULL:v14p170/r9.anchor: يقال : نقمت أنقم إذا بالغت في كراهية الشيء

RAZI-FULL:v14p170#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v14p170#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v14p170#2/r1.claim: Ifrāgh literally means pouring, as when a vessel is emptied into a mold; patience is metaphorically poured out like liquid.
RAZI-FULL:v14p170#2/r1.anchor: معنى الإفراغ في اللغة الصب . يقال : درهم مفرغ إذا كان مصبوبا في قالبه وليس بمضروب

RAZI-FULL:v14p170#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v14p170#2/r2.speaker: مجاهد
RAZI-FULL:v14p170#2/r2.claim: Mujāhid says they ask God to pour patience over them during crucifixion and amputation.
RAZI-FULL:v14p170#2/r2.anchor: قال مجاهد : المعنى صب علينا الصبر عند الصلب والقطع

RAZI-FULL:v14p170#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v14p170#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v14p170#2/r3.claim: Asking for patience to be poured out is stronger than asking for it to be sent down, since it requests all of it rather than some.
RAZI-FULL:v14p170#2/r3.anchor: { أفرغ علينا صبرا } أكمل من قوله : أنزل علينا صبرا

RAZI-FULL:v14p170#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v14p170#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v14p170#2/r4.claim: The indefinite word ṣabran signifies complete and perfect patience, as hayātan in 2:96 signifies a complete life.
RAZI-FULL:v14p170#2/r4.anchor: قوله { صبرا } مذكور بصيغة التنكير ، وذلك يدل على الكمال والتمام

RAZI-FULL:v14p170#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v14p170#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v14p170#2/r5.claim: Their request attributes their patience to God's creation and decree, since they ask Him for an act that is theirs.
RAZI-FULL:v14p170#2/r5.anchor: إن ذلك الصبر من قبلهم ومن أعمالهم ، ثم إنهم طلبوه من الله تعالى ، وذلك يدل على أن فعل العبد لا يحصل إلا بتخليق الله وقضائه

RAZI-FULL:v14p170#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v14p170#2/r6.speaker: القاضي
RAZI-FULL:v14p170#2/r6.claim: Al-Qāḍī says they ask for divine لطف that would prompt them to remain steadfast.
RAZI-FULL:v14p170#2/r6.anchor: قال القاضي : إنما سألوه تعالى الألطاف التي تدعوهم إلى الثبات والصبر

RAZI-FULL:v14p170#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v14p170#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v14p170#2/r7.claim: The author rejects al-Qāḍī's interpretation as contrary to the apparent wording: decisive motives come from God, so the action as a whole comes from Him.
RAZI-FULL:v14p170#2/r7.anchor: والجواب : هذا عدول عن الظاهر ، ثم الدليل يأباه ، وذلك لأن الفعل لا يحصل إلا عند حصول الداعية الجازمة

RAZI-FULL:v14p170#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v14p170#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v14p170#2/r8.claim: To die Muslims means to die upon the true religion Moses brought; the author argues faith and Islam only occur by God's creation, against the Muʿtazilite appeal to لطف.
RAZI-FULL:v14p170#2/r8.anchor: فمعناه توفنا على الدين الحق الذي جاء به موسى عليه السلام

RAZI-FULL:v14p170#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v14p170#2/r9.speaker: القاضي
RAZI-FULL:v14p170#2/r9.claim: Al-Qāḍī argues that because the magicians first identify their belief in the signs and then ask to die Muslims, Islam and faith are one and the same.
RAZI-FULL:v14p170#2/r9.anchor: احتج القاضي بهذه الآية على أن الإيمان والإسلام واحد

SAMIN-DURR:7:126/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:126/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:126/r1.claim: The verb تنقم has two forms and its government with من was explained at al-Maida 5:59; the construction uses تضمين.
SAMIN-DURR:7:126/r1.anchor: قد تقدم أن فيه لغتين وكيفية تعديه ب " من " ، وأنه على التضمين، في سورة المائدة

SAMIN-DURR:7:126/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:126/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:126/r2.claim: إلا أن آمنا can be an object: you find fault with us only for believing.
SAMIN-DURR:7:126/r2.anchor: يجوز أن يكون في محل نصب مفعولا به، أي: ما تعيب علينا إلا إيماننا

SAMIN-DURR:7:126/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:126/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:126/r3.claim: It can instead state the reason: you attack and punish us for no cause except our faith; either analysis is a restrictive, emptied exception.
SAMIN-DURR:7:126/r3.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون مفعولا من أجله، أي: ما تنال منا وتعذبنا لشيء من الأشياء إلا لإيماننا

SAMIN-DURR:7:126/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:126/r4.speaker: الفارسي
SAMIN-DURR:7:126/r4.claim: He takes لما جاءتنا temporally, governed by آمنا, meaning they believed when the signs arrived; this is also one view of Sibawayh.
SAMIN-DURR:7:126/r4.anchor: يجوز أن تكون ظرفية كما هو رأي الفارسي وأحد قولي سيبويه. والعامل فيها على هذا " آمنا

SAMIN-DURR:7:126/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:126/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:126/r5.claim: Alternatively لما means when-with-required-result; the omitted result is that when the signs came, they believed without hesitation.
SAMIN-DURR:7:126/r5.anchor: وأن تكون حرف وجوب لوجوب، وعلى هذا فلا بد لها من جواب وهو محذوف تقديره: لما جاءتنا آمنا بها

STUDYQURAN:7:111/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:111/r8.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:111/r8.claim: The reward language is worldly on its face but ambiguously foreshadows spiritual victory: the defeated sorcerers submit to God and will be rewarded by Him.
STUDYQURAN:7:111/r8.anchor: their subsequent submission to God and to Moses can be understood as a spiritual “victory,” for which they will surely have a reward with God

STUDYQURAN:7:111/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:111/r9.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:111/r9.claim: Pharaoh's phrase “brought nigh” also describes prophets, angels, and the most righteous in the highest Paradise; the later verses suggest the sorcerers were martyred.
STUDYQURAN:7:111/r9.anchor: it is noteworthy that Pharaoh’s promise that they shall be among those brought nigh

STUDYQURAN:7:111/r42.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:111/r42.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:111/r42.claim: The sorcerers' charge that Pharaoh seeks vengeance merely for faith resembles a believer at Pharaoh's court and Quranic condemnations of such persecution.
STUDYQURAN:7:111/r42.anchor: is similar to the words of a secret believer in Pharaoh’s court who asks Pharaoh if he would kill a man for saying, “My Lord is God”

STUDYQURAN:7:111/r43.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:111/r43.speaker: R
STUDYQURAN:7:111/r43.claim: The signs of the Lord for which Pharaoh takes vengeance are the feats Moses performed.
STUDYQURAN:7:111/r43.anchor: The signs of our Lord refers to the feats performed by Moses (R)

STUDYQURAN:7:111/r44.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:111/r44.speaker: Ṭ, Ṭs
STUDYQURAN:7:111/r44.claim: Their request for patience asks God to keep them steadfast through torture and death, lest duress return them to disbelief; the same prayer appears before Goliath's army.
STUDYQURAN:7:111/r44.anchor: a request that God aid them in remaining steadfast in the face of torture and death at the hands of Pharaoh, lest they revert to disbelief under this extreme duress

STUDYQURAN:7:111/r45.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:111/r45.speaker: Z
STUDYQURAN:7:111/r45.claim: Some say the painful death purified the sorcerers of their past sins.
STUDYQURAN:7:111/r45.anchor: According to some, the painful death suffered by the sorcerers purified them of their past sins (Z)

STUDYQURAN:7:111/r46.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:111/r46.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:111/r46.claim: Muslimīn here means submitters universally, those who fully submit to the One God.
STUDYQURAN:7:111/r46.anchor: used here in the universal sense of those who submit themselves fully to the One God

STUDYQURAN:7:111/r47.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:111/r47.speaker: IK, Ṭ, Ṭs
STUDYQURAN:7:111/r47.claim: Pharaoh reportedly killed and crucified them that day; early commentators say they began as sorcerers and ended as martyrs.
STUDYQURAN:7:111/r47.anchor: Pharaoh reportedly had the sorcerers killed and crucified that very day, and several early commentators observed that the sorcerers “began the day as sorcerers and ended it as martyrs”

STUDYQURAN:7:111/r48.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:111/r48.speaker: R
STUDYQURAN:7:111/r48.claim: The final request may mean “take us to Thyself as submitters,” a plea for immediate death to escape Pharaoh's punishment.
STUDYQURAN:7:111/r48.anchor: can also be translated “take us to Thyself as submitters” and might therefore be understood as a plea for God to take them to Himself immediately

TAB-FULL:v10p363#3/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p363#3/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v10p363#3/r1.claim: The magicians say they will return to God; their signs are proofs beyond Pharaoh’s power, and they ask God to sustain them through torture and take them as Muslims on Abraham’s religion.
TAB-FULL:v10p363#3/r1.anchor: يعني بالانقلاب إلى الله الرجوع إليه والمصير.

TAB-FULL:v10p363#3/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p363#3/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v10p363#3/r2.claim: Their request to have patience poured upon them asks for restraint that will keep them from renouncing God during Pharaoh’s torture.
TAB-FULL:v10p363#3/r2.anchor: يعنون بقولهم: أفرغ: أنزل علينا حبسا يحبسنا عن الكفر بك عند تعذيب فرعون إيانا.

TAB-FULL:v10p363#3/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p363#3/r3.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v10p363#3/r3.claim: Al-Suddi says Pharaoh killed and crucified the magicians.
TAB-FULL:v10p363#3/r3.anchor: عن السدي: {لأقطعن أيديكم وأرجلكم من خلاف} [الأعراف: 124] فقتلهم وصلبهم،

TAB-FULL:v10p363#3/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p363#3/r4.speaker: عبيد بن عمير
TAB-FULL:v10p363#3/r4.claim: Ubayd ibn Umayr says they were magicians in the morning and martyrs by evening.
TAB-FULL:v10p363#3/r4.anchor: عن عبيد بن عمير، قال: «كانت السحرة أول النهار سحرة، وآخر النهار شهداء»

TAB-FULL:v10p363#3/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p363#3/r5.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v10p363#3/r5.claim: Qatada reports that they became martyrs on the same day they had been magicians.
TAB-FULL:v10p363#3/r5.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: " {وألقي السحرة ساجدين} [الأعراف: 120] قال: ذكر لنا أنهم كانوا في أول النهار سحرة، وآخره شهداء "

TAB-FULL:v10p363#3/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p363#3/r6.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v10p363#3/r6.claim: Mujahid likewise describes their transformation from magicians to martyrs within the day.
TAB-FULL:v10p363#3/r6.anchor: عن ابن جريج، عن مجاهد: " {ربنا أفرغ علينا صبرا وتوفنا مسلمين} [الأعراف: 126] قال: كانوا أول النهار سحرة، وآخره شهداء "

ZAJJAJ:v2p367/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p367/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p367/r1.claim: أفرغ علينا صبرا means encompass or cover us with patience.

TABATABAI:7:125-126/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:125-126/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:125-126/r2.claim: The signs that prompted their belief may include the staff becoming a serpent, swallowing their ropes and staffs successively, then returning to its original form.
TABATABAI:7:125-126/r2.anchor: لاشتماله على جهات كل منها آية كصيرورتها ثعبانا

TABATABAI:7:125-126/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:125-126/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:125-126/r3.claim: Naqima means to dislike or abhor something.

TABATABAI:7:125-126/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:125-126/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:125-126/r4.claim: The converts, undeterred by threatened torture and death, ask God to pour patience over them and let them die in submission; the pouring metaphor pictures selves as vessels filled with patience like water.

TABRISI:7:123-126/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:123-126/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:7:123-126/r6.claim: The magicians say they will return to God with monotheism and sincerity; their return is to His recompense, and remembering reward steadies them while they answer Pharaoh’s threat with confidence in God’s harsher punishment.
TABRISI:7:123-126/r6.anchor: أي راجعون إلى ربنا بالتوحيد والإخلاص عن ابن عباس والانقلاب إلى الله تعالى

TABRISI:7:123-126/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:123-126/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:7:123-126/r7.claim: They say Pharaoh finds nothing to punish except their faith in God’s signs that Moses brought, which they recognized as from God and beyond anyone but Him to produce.
TABRISI:7:123-126/r7.anchor: قال ابن عباس: معناه ما لنا عندك من ذنب ولا ركبنا منك مكروها

TABRISI:7:123-126/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:123-126/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:123-126/r8.claim: Crucifixion derives from fastening someone to wood and all Qurʾānic readers double its lām; na-qima can mean punish or object, while “punishment” contrasts with a blameworthy injury. Ifrāgh is pouring out, and ṣabr is restraining visible despair; patience for truth is honor.
TABRISI:7:123-126/r8.anchor: الصلب الشد على الخشبة وغيرها وأصله من صلابة الشيء والقراء كلهم على تشديد اللام

TABRISI:7:126/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:126/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:126/r1.claim: Their prayer asks God to pour patience over them during amputation and crucifixion: aid them to endure bravely without fear or apostasy.
TABRISI:7:126/r1.anchor: أي أصبب علينا الصبر عند القطع والصلب حتى لا نرجع كفارا

TABRISI:7:126/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:126/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:126/r2.claim: “Take us as Muslims” means keep them steadfast in faith until death; another interpretation asks to remain sincerely devoted so persecution will not turn them from their religion.
TABRISI:7:126/r2.anchor: أي وفقنا للثبات على الإيمان والإسلام إلى وقت الوفاة

TABRISI:7:126/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:126/r3.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:7:126/r3.claim: One account says Pharaoh crucified them that very day, making them martyrs after they had been magicians that morning; another says he never reached them because God protected them.
TABRISI:7:126/r3.anchor: قالوا فصلبهم فرعون من يومه فكانوا أول النهار كفارا سحرة وآخر النهار شهداء بررة

THALABI:v4p270/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p270/r9.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p270/r9.claim: The sorcerers tell Pharaoh that his only grievance against them is their belief in their Lord’s signs when they came to them.
THALABI:v4p270/r9.anchor: وما تنقم منا قرأ العامة بكسر القاف

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p288#3/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p288#3/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p288#3/r1.claim: Naqima means to intensely dislike something, with the phrase discussed at 5:59.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p288#3/r1.anchor: يقال: نقمت أنقم إذا بالغت في كراهية الشيء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p288#3/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p288#3/r2.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p288#3/r2.claim: The magicians say they have committed no offense or harm against Pharaoh that merits punishment, except believing in the signs.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p288#3/r2.anchor: ما لنا عندك من ذنب ولا ركبنا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p288#3/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p288#3/r3.speaker: الضحاك
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p288#3/r3.claim: Pharaoh reproaches them only for believing Moses’ signs, the staff and hand, came from God, since no one else could produce them.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p288#3/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p288#3/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p288#3/r4.claim: Ifrāgh literally means pouring out a vessel’s whole contents; patience is pictured as poured over and surrounding them.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p288#3/r4.anchor: وأصله من إفراغ الإناء؛ وهو صب ما فيه أجمع حتى يخلو الإناء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p288#3/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p288#3/r5.speaker: مجاهد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p288#3/r5.claim: They ask for patience during crucifixion and amputation so they will not revert to disbelief.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p288#3/r5.anchor: اصبب علينا الصبر عند الصلب والقطع حتى لا نرجع كفارا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p288#3/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p288#3/r6.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p288#3/r6.claim: They ask God to send down patience that surrounds them, matching the encompassing image of pouring.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p290/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p290/r1.speaker: مجاهد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p290/r1.claim: They ask to die with sincere devotion in worship.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p290/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p290/r2.speaker: ابن كيسان
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p290/r2.claim: They ask to die adhering to Moses’ religion.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:126-127/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:126-127/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:126-127/r1.claim: They say Pharaoh resents them only because they believed in the signs Moses brought, the staff and the hand.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:126-127/r1.anchor: ما أتى به موسى من العصا واليد

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:126-127/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:126-127/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:126-127/r2.claim: They pray for patience under crucifixion and mutilation so they will not return to disbelief, and for death as Muslims following Moses’ religion.

ELMALILI:7:126/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:126/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:126/r1.claim: The magicians say Pharaoh resents only their belief in the Lord's signs; accepting evident truth is a virtue, not a crime deserving punishment.
ELMALILI:7:126/r1.anchor: Hâlbuki sen bizden hiçbir sebeple değil, ancak Rabbimizin âyetlerine

ELMALILI:7:126/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:126/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:126/r2.claim: They say their recognition of truth is fixed in conscience and cannot be abandoned to please Pharaoh, whose anger exposes injustice and ignorance.
ELMALILI:7:126/r2.anchor: vicdanlarımızda def‘i nâkābil bir zarûret ile sâbit olan böyle bir idrak ve imandan seni memnun etmek için vazgeçmek de tâkatimizden hâriç bulunduğu hâlde

ELMALILI:7:126/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:126/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:126/r3.claim: Their prayer asks for patience that will flood and cleanse them, keeping them pure from disbelief, idolatry, deceit, and sin.
ELMALILI:7:126/r3.anchor: yâ Rabbenâ bize sabır ifâza et yani su gibi her tarafımızı kaplayacak; şirk ü küfr, mekr ü isyan küfürlerinden yıkayacak

ELMALILI:7:126/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:126/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:126/r4.claim: Asking to die as Muslims demonstrates the depth and certainty of their faith and their disregard for death.
ELMALILI:7:126/r4.anchor: imanlarındaki ciddiyeti, îkānlarındaki şiddet ü kuvveti ölümü istihfaf

ELMALILI:7:126/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:126/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
ELMALILI:7:126/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that they were magicians in the morning and martyrs by evening; others argued the threat was not carried out because the Qur'an does not state it explicitly, while the author favors its fulfillment from the Qur'anic context.
ELMALILI:7:126/r5.anchor: Bazıları İbn Abbas’tan “günün evvelinde sâhir idiler, âhirinde şehit oldular” diye nakletmiş

ELMALILI:7:126/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:126/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:126/r6.claim: The author prefers that Pharaoh executed them: they knowingly remained steadfast and welcomed martyrdom, which also established the sincerity of their faith and the miracle's truth.
ELMALILI:7:126/r6.anchor: Lâkin bizce siyâk-ı Kur’an vukū‘unu andırıyor. Bu zevât, imanlarında sebat ederek ölmeyi canlarına minnet bilmişler ve hak yolunda şehid olmuşlardır

ELMALILI:7:126/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:126/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:126/r7.claim: Their martyrdom did not frustrate Moses' miracle, whose purpose was to prove his truth; their actual self-sacrifice made the sincerity of their testimony unmistakable.
ELMALILI:7:126/r7.anchor: Mucizenin gayesi de Mûsâ’nın davasındaki sıdkını isbat idi

ELMALILI:7:126/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:126/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:126/r8.claim: Pharaoh's propaganda and terror still affected his people, showing that deceit can have a temporary effect even against truth.
ELMALILI:7:126/r8.anchor: Firavun’un mekr propagandası ve zulm ü tedhiş siyaseti de kavmi üzerinde icrâ-yı te’sîrden hâlî kalmadığını

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p141/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p141/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p141/r1.claim: The magicians' return to God expresses surrender, reliance, and confidence that He will reward them for their suffering on Judgment Day.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p141/r1.anchor: هذا تسليم واتكال على الله تعالى وثقة بما عنده والمعنى إنا نرجع إلى ثواب ربنا يوم الجزاء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p141/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p141/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p141/r2.claim: Another possible sense is that they will meet God, receive His mercy, and be delivered from Pharaoh and his company.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p141/r2.anchor: أو إنا ننقلب إلى لقاء ربنا ورحمته وخلاصنا منك ومن لقائك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p141/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p141/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p141/r3.claim: A further reading is that death is inevitable, so they do not fear it because Pharaoh can only bring about what must happen to them.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p141/r3.anchor: أو إنا ميتون منقلبون إلى الله فلا نبالي بالموت إذ لا تقدر أن تفعل بنا إلا ما لا بد لنا منه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p141/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p141/r4.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p141/r4.claim: Al-Zamakhshari allows the pronoun to include both the magicians and Pharaoh returning to God for judgment, but Abu Hayyan rejects this reading.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p141/r4.anchor: والذي أجاز هذا الوجه هو الزمخشري

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p141/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p141/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p141/r5.claim: The inclusive reading is unlikely because the pronoun in “what do you resent against us” refers specifically to the believing magicians; consistent pronouns favor that scope.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p141/r5.anchor: فإن هذا الضمير يخص مؤمني السحرة والأولى اتحاد الضمائر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p141/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p141/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p141/r6.claim: Their phrase “to our Lord” disavows Pharaoh and his claim to lordship.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p141/r6.anchor: وفي قولهم إلى ربنا تبرؤ من فرعون ومن ربوبيته

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p141/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p141/r7.speaker: الكرماني
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p141/r7.claim: Al-Karmani explains that this surah condenses Pharaoh's story while al-Shu'ara expands it from his reminder of Moses' upbringing through the drowning of his people.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p141/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p141/r8.speaker: الضحاك
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p141/r8.claim: Al-Dahhak takes تنقم منا to mean that Pharaoh finds fault with them.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p141/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p141/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p141/r9.claim: Other interpreters gloss the phrase as what Pharaoh dislikes, blames, or counts as a punishable sin in them.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p141/r9.anchor: وقال غيره: وما تكره منا، وقال الزمخشري: وما تعيب منا، وقال ابن عطية: وما تعد علينا ذنبا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p141/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p141/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p141/r10.claim: Under the fault-finding glosses, “except that we believed” is the object of تنقم in a free exception construction; comparable wording occurs elsewhere in the Qur'an.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p141/r10.anchor: وعلى هذه التأويلات يكون قوله إلا أن آمنا في موضع المفعول ويكون من الاستثناء المفرغ من المفعول

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p141/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p141/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p141/r11.claim: Abu Hayyan prefers construing تنقم منا as “inflict harm on us,” since the preposition من suggests what Pharaoh brings upon them, as in ينتقم الله منه.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p141/r11.anchor: والذي يظهر من تعديته بمن أن المعنى وما تنقم منا أي ما تنال منا كقوله فينتقم الله منه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p141/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p141/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p141/r12.claim: On the preferred sense, forms نقم and انتقم share a meaning, and the exception is causal: their only alleged offense is belief in God's signs.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p141/r12.anchor: على هذا يكون قوله إلا أن آمنا مفعولا من أجله واستثناء مفرغا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p141/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p141/r13.speaker: عطاء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p141/r13.claim: Ata paraphrases the statement as denying any offense that merits punishment other than their belief.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p141/r13.anchor: قال عطاء: أي ما لنا عندك ذنب تعذبنا عليه إلا أنا آمنا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p141/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p141/r14.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p141/r14.claim: The signs are the miracles Moses brought; the believers' reply refutes Pharaoh's divinity and disowns their former belief in him, affirming faith as the root of honor.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p141/r14.anchor: والآيات المعجزات التي أتى بها موسى عليه السلام

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p141/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p141/r15.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p141/r15.claim: If لما is temporal, آمنا is its governing verb; if لما is a particle, its omitted response is understood as “when they came, we believed.”
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p141/r15.anchor: ومن جعل لما ظرفا جعل العامل فيها أن آمنا ومن جعلها حرفا جعل جوابها محذوفا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p142/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p142/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p142/r1.claim: A cited poetic line illustrates the exception pattern in which there is no fault except a flaw left on swords from striking battle ranks.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p142/r1.anchor: ولا عيب فيهم غير أن سيوفهم ... بهن فلول من قراع الكتائب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p142/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p142/r2.speaker: الحسن، وأبو حيوة، وأبو اليسر هاشم، وابن أبي عبلة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p142/r2.claim: These readers pronounce the qaf in تنقم with fatḥ, using the dialectal imperfect naqama; the majority reading is more eloquent.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p142/r2.anchor: قرأ الحسن وأبو حيوة وأبو اليسر هاشم وابن أبي عبلة وما تنقم بفتح القاف

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p142/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p142/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p142/r3.claim: When threatened with cutting and crucifixion, the believers ask God for patience if the punishment occurs; the request does not prove it actually did.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p142/r3.anchor: لما أوعدهم بالقطع والصلب سألوا الله تعالى أن يرزقهم الصبر على ما يحل بهم إن حل وليس في هذا السؤال ما يدل على وقوع هذا الموعد بهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p142/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p142/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p142/r4.claim: Abu Hayyan rejects the inference that asking to die as Muslims proves the threatened punishment was not inflicted; they ask God to take them, rather than to die by cutting and crucifixion.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p142/r4.anchor: ولا في قوله وتوفنا مسلمين دليل على أنه لم يحل بهم الموعود خلافا لمن قال يدل على ذلك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p142/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p142/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p142/r5.claim: Their request is to die in Islam, meaning submission to God's religion and commands.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p142/r5.anchor: سألوا الموت على الإسلام وهو الانقياد إلى دين الله وما أمر به

ALUSI-FULL:v9p28#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p28#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p28#2/r1.claim: Tanqimu means to dislike or reproach; its past forms are given on the patterns of daraba and ʿalima.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p28#2/r1.anchor: وجاء في الماضي نقم ونقم على وزن ضرب وعلم

ALUSI-FULL:v9p28#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p28#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p28#2/r2.claim: 'From us' means the company that believed; the exception is an absolute exception, with its verbal noun as object, explaining that their only supposed fault is believing God's signs.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p28#2/r2.anchor: منا ( معشر من آمن : ( إلا أن آمنا بأيات ربنا لما جاءتنا

ALUSI-FULL:v9p28#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p28#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p28#2/r3.claim: A cited poetic construction likewise says there is no flaw except that guests are distracted by longing for loved ones and homeland; it illustrates the exception's syntax.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p28#2/r3.anchor: ولا عيب فيهم غير أن ضيوفهم تعاب بنسيان الأحبة والوطن

ALUSI-FULL:v9p28#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p28#2/r4.speaker: عطاء
ALUSI-FULL:v9p28#2/r4.claim: A report from Ata takes tanqimu as 'punish'; then believing is the cause of their punishment, and on either reading the believers cut off Pharaoh's hope that his threat will succeed.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p28#2/r4.anchor: يشير ماروى عن عطاء وعليه فيكون

ALUSI-FULL:v9p28#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p28#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p28#2/r5.claim: Their prayer for God to pour patience over them compares patience to poured water; alternatively they ask for what purifies their sins by helping them endure Pharaoh's threat.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p28#2/r5.anchor: أي أفض علينا صبرا يغمرنا كما يفرغ الماء أو صب علينا ما يطهرنا من الآثام وهو الصبر على وعيد فرعون

ALUSI-FULL:v9p28#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p28#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p28#2/r6.claim: On the first reading, 'pour' is an explicit derivative metaphor and 'patience' its contextual indicator; on the second, patience is an original concealed metaphor and 'pour' its imaginative elaboration.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p28#2/r6.anchor: على الأول استعارة تبعية تصريحية و ( صبرا ) قرينتها والمراد هب لنا صبرا تاما كثيرا

ALUSI-FULL:v9p28#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p28#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p28#2/r7.claim: The suggestion that both readings work alike through the idea of flooding or purification is judged unconvincing, despite the stature of its proponent.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p28#2/r7.anchor: وقيل : الكلام على الأول كالكلام على الثاني إلا أن الجامع هناك الغمر وههنا التطهير

ALUSI-FULL:v9p28#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p28#2/r8.speaker: ابن عباس والكلبي والسدي
ALUSI-FULL:v9p28#2/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas, al-Kalbi and al-Suddi say 'take us in death as Muslims' asks God to keep them firm in Islam and not let Pharaoh's threat tempt them away; they report that Pharaoh carried out his threat.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p28#2/r8.anchor: عن ابن عباس والكلبي والسدي أنه فعل بهم ما أوعدهم به

ALUSI-FULL:v9p28#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p28#2/r9.speaker: some exegetes
ALUSI-FULL:v9p28#2/r9.claim: Others say Pharaoh could not carry out the threat because God promised Moses, Aaron, and their followers victory; the first group says victory may mean victory in argument or the final outcome, without excluding some deaths.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p28#2/r9.anchor: لقوله تعالى : ( لايصلون إليكما بآياتنا أنتما ومن اتبعكما الغالبون )

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p266#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p266#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p266#2/r2.claim: Tanqimu means what you dislike about us; al-Dahhak and others gloss it as faulting us, while ʿAta says they had no offense meriting punishment except believing in God's signs.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p266#2/r2.anchor: {وما تنقم منا} أي: ما تكره منا. وقال الضحاك وغيره: وما تطعن علينا.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p266#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p266#2/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p266#2/r3.claim: Faced with Pharaoh, they turn to God asking Him to pour patience on them and take them as Muslims.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p266#2/r3.anchor: ثم فزعوا إلى الله عز وجل فقالوا: {ربنا أفرغ} اصبب، {علينا صبرا وتوفنا مسلمين}

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p266#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p266#2/r4.speaker: الكلبي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p266#2/r4.claim: Al-Kalbi says Pharaoh cut off their hands and feet and crucified them; another view says he could not, because God promised the believers victory in another verse.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p266#2/r4.anchor: ذكر الكلبي: أن فرعون قطع أيديهم وأرجلهم وصلبهم وذكر غيره: أنه لم يقدر عليهم

BAYDAWI-FULL:7:126/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:126/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:126/r1.claim: Tanqimu means reproach; the only reproach is belief in God's signs, the best deed and root of virtues, which they will not abandon for Pharaoh.
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:126/r1.anchor: وما تنقم منا } وما تنكر منا. { إلا أن ءامنا بئايت ربنا لما جاءتنا } وهو خير الأعمال وأصل المناقب

BAYDAWI-FULL:7:126/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:126/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:126/r2.claim: They ask God to pour patience over them like water or pour what cleanses sin by enabling them to endure Pharaoh's threat.
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:126/r2.anchor: أفض علينا صبرا يغمرنا كما يفرغ الماء، أو صب علينا ما يطهرنا من الآثام وهو الصبر على وعيد فرعون.

BAYDAWI-FULL:7:126/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:126/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:126/r3.claim: To die Muslim means to remain steadfast in Islam; one view says Pharaoh carried out his threat, another says he could not seize them.
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:126/r3.anchor: وتوفنا مسلمين } ثابتين على الإسلام. قيل إنه فعل بهم ما أوعدهم به. وقيل إنه لم يقدر عليهم

BIQAI-FULL:v3p85/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p85/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p85/r3.claim: The only grievance Pharaoh has against them is their faith in God’s signs, which came from their benefactor and therefore called for gratitude, not punishment.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p85/r3.anchor: أي فعلك ذلك بنا وتعيب علينا

BIQAI-FULL:v3p85/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p85/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p85/r4.claim: They did not delay once the proof of truth arrived; that prompt recognition should earn honor rather than vengeance.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p85/r4.anchor: أي حين { جاءتنا } لم نتأخر عن معرفة الصدق المصدق , وهذا يوجب الإكرام لا الانتقام

BIQAI-FULL:v3p85/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p85/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p85/r5.claim: They pray for encompassing patience under the threat and to have their souls taken while fully and inwardly submitted to the truth.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p85/r5.anchor: أي اقبض أرواحنا وافية حال كوننا { مسلمين * }

BIQAI-FULL:v3p85/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p85/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p85/r6.claim: God apparently answered their prayer, alluded to through their address to Him as Lord, by not empowering Pharaoh to carry out the threat.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p85/r6.anchor: والظاهر أن الله تعالى أجابهم فيما سألوه تلويحا بذكر الرب فلم يقدره عليهم

QUSHAYRI:v1p347/r1.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p347/r1.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p347/r1.claim: The magicians' apparent victory was only a ruse; divine power overturned it, defeated their schemes, and frustrated their hope.
QUSHAYRI:v1p347/r1.anchor: فبيناهم في توهم أن الغلبة لهم

QUSHAYRI:v1p347/r2.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p347/r2.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p347/r2.claim: God disclosed inward love beneath outward enmity and can reverse who appears friend or foe, while bringing the decreed outcome to pass.
QUSHAYRI:v1p347/r2.anchor: على الوهلة فأصبحوا في صدر العداوة

QUSHAYRI:v1p347/r3.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p347/r3.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p347/r3.claim: The believers' inward secrets had left the prison of forms, their hearts were cleansed of imagined separation, and gnosis had dawned within them.
QUSHAYRI:v1p347/r3.anchor: وأن قلوبهم طهرت عن توهم التفرقة

QUSHAYRI:v1p347/r4.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p347/r4.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p347/r4.claim: They witnessed God with sound insight, so the self's threats no longer ruled them and no pretext remained between them and God.
QUSHAYRI:v1p347/r4.anchor: ولم يبق لتخويفات النفس فيهم سلطان

QUSHAYRI:v1p347/r5.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p347/r5.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p347/r5.claim: Because their destination was God, the hardships they met on the way to Him became easy to bear.
QUSHAYRI:v1p347/r5.anchor: لما كان مصيرهم إلى الله سهل عليهم ما لقوا في مسيرهم إلى الله

QUSHAYRI:v1p347/r6.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p347/r6.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p347/r6.claim: Those who act and suffer for God seek His aid sincerely; the way of one devoted wholly to God is to rely wholly on Him.
QUSHAYRI:v1p347/r6.anchor: كذا سنة من كان الله أن يكون كله على الله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p57/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p57/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p57/r1.claim: The Qur’an’s aim is not to reconstruct historical events; exegetes’ efforts to determine exactly how Pharaoh’s threat played out add nothing to the verse’s lesson at 79:26.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p57/r1.anchor: وليس من غرض القرآن معرفة الحوادث كما قال في سورة النازعات ( 26 ) إن في ذلك لعبرة لمن يخشى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p57/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p57/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p57/r2.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr’s apparent reading is that Pharaoh was silenced when he saw how little the believers cared about his threat.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p57/r2.anchor: والظاهر أن فرعون أفحم لما رأى قلة مبالاتهم بوعيده فلم يرد جوابا .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p57/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p57/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p57/r3.claim: Their use of ‘Muslims’ in prayer shows that God inspired them to recognize the religion of the prophets and the ṣiddīqūn since Abraham.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p57/r3.anchor: وذكرهم الإسلام في دعائهم يدل على أن الله ألهمهم حقيقته التي كان عليها النبيون والصديقون من عهد إبراهيم عليه السلام .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p57/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p57/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p57/r4.claim: ‘Muslims’ is the Qur’an’s wording for their prayer to die in the state of the ṣiddīqūn; the term Islam encompasses that state, as discussed at 2:132.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p57/r4.anchor: والظاهر أن كلمة مسلمين } تعبير القرآن عن دعائهم بأن يتوفاهم الله على حالة الصديقين

JISHUMI:v4p2678/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2678/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2678/r1.claim: The magicians inferred God's oneness and the truth of prophethood, then believed.
JISHUMI:v4p2678/r1.anchor: الآية تدل على أن السحرة استدلوا على التوحيد والنبوات فصدقوا وآمنوا.

JISHUMI:v4p2678/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2678/r2.speaker: أبو علي
JISHUMI:v4p2678/r2.claim: Their answer to Pharaoh proves sincere faith; God answered their prayer, and they died Muslims and entered Paradise.
JISHUMI:v4p2678/r2.anchor: قال أبو علي: فأجاب الله دعاءهم وتوفوا مسلمين وصاروا إلى الجنة.

JISHUMI:v4p2678/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2678/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2678/r3.claim: Their request to die as Muslims shows that reward is attained through Islam.
JISHUMI:v4p2678/r3.anchor: وتدل على أن بالإسلام ينال الثواب؛ لذلك قال: وتوفنا مسلمين.

JISHUMI:v4p2678/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2678/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2678/r4.claim: When threatened by oppressors, people are obligated to be patient.
JISHUMI:v4p2678/r4.anchor: وتدل على أن الواجب عند وعيد الظلمة الصبر؛ لذلك قال: أفرغ علينا صبرا.

JISHUMI:v4p2678/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2678/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2678/r5.claim: In such a crisis, one must turn wholly to God to ward off oppression or receive recompense.
JISHUMI:v4p2678/r5.anchor: وتدل على أن الواجب عند ذلك الانقطاع إلى الله تعالى؛ ليدفع عنه الظلم أو يوفيه الجزاء.

JISHUMI:v4p2678/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2678/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2678/r6.claim: Their faith is their own act, and Pharaoh's threat is his act, invalidating the determinists' doctrine about human action.
JISHUMI:v4p2678/r6.anchor: وتدل على أن الإيمان فعلهم، وأن ما أوعدهم فرعون فعلة ليصح الكلام، فيبطل قول المجبرة في المخلوق [*].

THALABI:v4p270#2/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p270#2/r1.speaker: الحسن وابن المحيصن
THALABI:v4p270#2/r1.claim: They read نقم with fatḥa on qāf; both naqima yanqamu and naqima yanqimu are valid forms.
THALABI:v4p270#2/r1.anchor: وقرأ الحسن وابن [المحيصن] بفتح القاف وهما لغتان نقم ينقم ونقم ينقم.

THALABI:v4p270#2/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p270#2/r2.speaker: الشاعر
THALABI:v4p270#2/r2.claim: A cited poem witnesses the verb نقموا in the sense of taking offense or objecting.
THALABI:v4p270#2/r2.anchor: قال الشاعر: وما نقموا من بني أمية إلا … أنهم يحلمون إن غضبوا

THALABI:v4p270#2/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p270#2/r3.speaker: الضحاك وغيره
THALABI:v4p270#2/r3.claim: They explain the phrase as meaning what do they criticize us for?
THALABI:v4p270#2/r3.anchor: وقال الضحاك وغيره: يعني وما يطعن علينا.

THALABI:v4p270#2/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p270#2/r4.speaker: عطاء
THALABI:v4p270#2/r4.claim: He says the only alleged offense was believing God’s signs; the magicians ask God to pour patience on them through torture and execution so they die Muslims, changing from unbelieving sorcerers to righteous martyrs within one day.
THALABI:v4p270#2/r4.anchor: قال عطاء: ما لنا عندك من ذنب وما ارتكبنا منك مكروها تعذبنا عليه إلا أن آمنا بآيات ربنا لما جاءتنا

BAQILLANI:v1p243/r1.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p243/r1.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p243/r1.claim: Speech can depict inner thought and feeling through gesture, indication, or explicit eloquent wording; verbal expression and signs each have different degrees and levels.
BAQILLANI:v1p243/r1.anchor: وتصوير ما في النفس وتشكيل ما في القلب حتى تعلمه وكأنك مشاهده

BAQILLANI:v1p243/r2.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p243/r2.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p243/r2.claim: Description ranges from accurate portrayal to excess or shortfall, and varies in precision, beauty, brevity, explanation, completeness, and approximation.
BAQILLANI:v1p243/r2.anchor: ورب وصف يصور لك الموصوف كما هو على جهته لا خلف فيه ورب وصف ببر عليه ويتعداه

BAQILLANI:v1p243/r3.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p243/r3.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p243/r3.claim: He contrasts concise portrayal, as in the sleepers' fear, with extended exposition of the Resurrection's terrors; the detailed scenes make that Day vivid.
BAQILLANI:v1p243/r3.anchor: وهذا مما يصور الشيء على جهته ويمثل أهوال ذلك اليوم

BAQILLANI:v1p243/r4.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p243/r4.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p243/r4.claim: The sorcerers' answer to Pharaoh's threat is an instance of speech rendered within a scene; Baqillani links it to their parallel declaration that they return to God and hope for forgiveness.
BAQILLANI:v1p243/r4.anchor: إنا إلى ربنا منقلبون وما تنقم منا إلا أن آمنا
